title: Characterizations of torsion abelian sheaves on the etale site
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and $F\in\Ab(T_{\Et})$ an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The following are equivalent: (1) $F$ is torsion [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], i.e. the canonical map $c_F:\varinjlim_nF[n]\to F$ is an isomorphism; (2) every local section is locally killed by a positive integer: for every etale $U\to T$ and $s\in F(U)$ there are an etale covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $n_i\ge1$ with $n_i\,s|_{U_i}=0$; (3) for every geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point] $\bar t$ of $T$ the stalk $F_{\bar t}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a torsion abelian group. Moreover these conditions do not imply that every group $F(U)$ is torsion: if $T\neq\emptyset$, the constant sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on $T_{\Et}$ is torsion, while over the etale $T$-scheme $U=\coprod_{n\ge1}T$ (structure map the codiagonal) restriction along the coprojections is an isomorphism $\underline{\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z}(U)\cong\prod_{n\ge1}\underline{\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z}(T)$, and the section corresponding to $(\iota_T(1/2^n))_{n\ge1}$, where $\iota_T:\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z\to\underline{\mathbf Q/\mathbf Z}(T)$ is the canonical map from the constant presheaf to its sheafification, has infinite order.

proof.text: If the canonical colimit map is invertible, its kernel-inclusion cocone is colimiting. Positive integers ordered by divisibility are filtered (products give upper bounds). Apply the geometric stalk functor and Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep after shrinking the filtered-colimit preservation instance for the forgetful functor of AddCommGrpCat. Every stalk element is the image of an element of one kernel. Apply the additive stalk functor to kernel.condition and evaluate: the image is killed by that kernel index. This needs additivity, not preservation of kernels by stalks.

proof.text: Use the already proved tool AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isTorsion_iff_isAddTorsion_sheafFiber from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.EtaleTorsion for local torsion to stalk torsion. For the converse, apply Sheaf.IsTorsion.of_isAddTorsion_sheafFiber to the conservative family of lifted algebraic-closure points. Transfer the given algebraically closed stalk torsion through uliftSheafFiberIso. This specializes the source result to algebraically closed rather than separably closed fields, with no new hypothesis.

proof.text: For a locally torsion sheaf, form the positive-integer kernel diagram. Its comparison is monic: AB5 makes colim.map of the monic natural transformation to the constant diagram monic, and the constant diagram has colimit F because the index is connected. It is epic: local torsion supplies a covering and a positive annihilator for each restriction; the evaluation functor preserves kernels, and PreservesKernel.iso composed with AddCommGrpCat.kernelIsoKer gives a lift of each killed restriction. These lifts map into the colimit, proving local surjectivity. Sheaf.epi_of_isLocallySurjective and isIso_of_mono_of_epi finish. Combine with the preceding stalk characterization.

proof.text: A rational q modulo integral multiples of 1 is killed by its positive denominator: Rat.den_mul_eq_num identifies the multiple with q.num. Transfer this elementwise proof to ULift. Use the proved upstream Point.sheafFiberConstantSheafIso, built from sheafification invariance and the connected constant-diagram colimit. Its inverse is the global constant unit followed by the germ: Point.toPresheafFiber_presheafFiberConstIso_hom identifies the constant-presheaf germ with presheafFiberConstIso.inv by cancellation; Point.toPresheafFiber_naturality then identifies the composite. Shrink the forgetful filtered-colimit preservation instance to the point universe. Surjectivity transports torsion to each stalk, and the characterization proved above gives torsion of the constant sheaf.

proof.text: Construct U as the positive-integer coproduct of T with its etale codiagonal, using IsZariskiLocalAtSource.sigmaDesc, and j from the coprojections. sigmaOpenCover gives coverage. The existing closed tools isSheafFor_ofArrows and subsingleton_obj_of_isEmpty give bijectivity of restriction: separatedness gives injectivity; for surjectivity equal indices cancel a monic coprojection, and different indices force an empty test scheme by isEmpty_of_commSq_sigmaι_of_ne, hence compatibility. Glue the dyadic coordinates. For nonempty T choose its algebraic-closure point; the composite identified directly with the inverse of the proved upstream constant-stalk isomorphism makes the global unit injective. If k kills the glued section, restriction and injectivity force k/2^n to be integral for every n. Choose n=k+1; Nat.lt_two_pow_self gives 2^n>k, so the rational is strictly between 0 and 1. An integer cannot lie in this interval. Thus every positive k fails to kill the section.

split_report.summary: Stacks states no such lemma (Section 0DDB and Lemma 03SA (2) only use 'F = union of the F[n]'); the proof is agent-written from Stacks Definition 040R, Lemmas 03PR, 03PT, Theorem 03PU. Route chosen: (1)<=>(3) via stalks (step 1: the stalk functor is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] and commutes with colimits [lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits], so (c_F)_t is the inclusion of the torsion subgroup of F_t; step 2: conservativity [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative, Lean closed]); (2)<=>(3) directly from the description of stalk elements as triples (cofiltered neighbourhoods, Mathlib leaf), the lift of geometric points to coverings (Mathlib leaf, Stacks 03PR) and composition/cancellation of etale morphisms (Mathlib leaf), as in the proof of 03PU. This avoids the sheafification/locally-surjective description of colimits suggested in the brief (no AB5 or epi-iff-locally-surjective node is needed). The Q/Z example (steps 5-7) needs two new nodes: lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk (stalk of a constant etale sheaf is E; unsplit; slopmaster2 has the sorry-free CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.Point.sheafFiberConstantSheafIso for a general point) and lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-copies (Mathlib leaf: coproduct of copies of T, open coprojections, disjointness, codiagonal etale). Statement made precise (not changed in content): the 'section (1/2^n)_n' is now the section corresponding to (iota_T(1/2^n))_n under F(U) = prod F(T); def-weil-pbc-etale-site added to stmt_deps (coverings in (2)). The tool uses outside unit sk-def-pbc's route (sk-def-conv, sk-def-exchange): prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact (sk-prop-h2), lem-kun-stalks-commute-colimits (sk-prop-sf-kunneth-ordinary), lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative (sk-prop-cd, closed); all generic facts on stalks used as black boxes.
